commitResults.messageTitle: Merge remote-tracking branch 'ay2627/add-gradle-support'
Point the Gradle build at lumi.Lumi and name the JAR lumi.jar
Extract Ui to own all interaction with the user
Extract TaskList to own the tasks and guard access by position
Extract Parser to turn raw input into commands and tasks
Turn Lumi and Storage into objects with injected collaborators
commitResults.messageBody:
Lumi now takes its save path, builds the Ui, Storage and TaskList in a
constructor that neither reads nor prints, and runs the session in
run(). Storage holds that path as a field instead of a fixed constant,
so a caller can point it at any file.

Loading stays in run() rather than the constructor, so a load failure
is reported after the greeting instead of before it; the constructor
is left free of side effects. Parser keeps its static methods because
it holds no state.

Only the path constant and main() remain static in Lumi, down from 39
static members before this refactoring began. The text UI test confirms
output, saved data and reload are all unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move the remaining actions into Command classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Add ListCommand, MarkCommand, DeleteCommand and ExitCommand, which
empties listTasks, setTaskDone and deleteTask out of Lumi.

Split the dispatch in two: createCommand only chooses and builds a
command, executeCommand runs it and asks isExit() whether to carry on.
That drops the .execute(tasks, ui, storage) repeated in all eight
branches, and leaves createCommand as a pure function of the input,
ready to move into Parser next.

Lumi is down to 131 lines from 301 when this refactoring started. Also
removes a now-unused Task import and a duplicated Javadoc line. The
text UI test confirms output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let Parser build the command and reduce run() to the loop
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the dispatch switch and the eight command keywords into
Parser.parse(), which now takes a whole input line and returns the
command it names. Recognising a keyword and parsing its arguments are
two sides of the same job, so they belong together; parseCommandWord
and parseArguments become private now that only parse() calls them.

run() is the loop itself: read a line, parse it, execute it, ask
isExit(). That absorbs readCommandsUntilExit, executeInput,
executeCommand and createCommand, leaving Lumi at 81 lines from the
301 it started at.

The hasNextCommand() and isEmpty() guards are kept, unlike the sketch
in the brief: without the first the program throws when piped input
ends, which the text UI test relies on. Ui.show() already brackets
each block with divider lines, so showLine() is not adopted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find to search task descriptions for a keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
Split the work three ways: Task answers whether it matches, TaskList
returns the ones that do, and FindCommand shows them. Matching on the
description alone matters -- searching toString() would make 'find D'
hit every deadline through its type icon.

Task.hasKeyword() is used rather than exposing the description, so the
matching rule lives in one place and can later be made case-insensitive
without touching any caller.

Matches are numbered from 1 in their own right, as the brief shows; the
Javadoc notes those numbers are for reading, not for mark or delete.

Lumi is untouched: a whole new command needed only a command class and
one case in Parser. The unknown-command message now lists find, and the
text UI test covers matches, no match and a missing keyword.
